races.title: State Senate, District 29
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dave Craven
cands.bio: Republican state senator from Asheboro. Appointed to the North Carolina Senate in July 2020 and has served since, representing District 26 and then District 29. Senior vice president for business development at Fidelity Bank. Former Randolph County Republican Party chairman.

controversies.text: In March 2026 the News & Observer reported that Craven's campaign paid nearly $59,000 to a firm owned by lobbyist Kevin Wilkinson's wife. A watchdog found over 20% of his last-election money came from people tied to Wilkinson's clients. Craven called her a longtime friend who planned campaign events. A state senator asked officials to investigate. No finding has been reported.

endorsements.text: The Civic Table (Sway voting group by Carrie Jackson) listed him in its 2026 voter guide recommendations, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or documented action by Craven on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, or red-flag laws. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year. We could not confirm where he grew up or his exact birth date. His campaign site gives general statements on the Second Amendment and the Right to Life but no specific bills or policies. We found no official finding on the 2026 allegations about his lobbyist-linked fundraising.

local.label: Roots 80: He was born in Randolph County and calls himself a native of the county. The record shows him living and working there as an adult since at least 2016, and he now lives in Asheboro; where he grew up is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2020, with Finance Committee leadership. Fidelity Bank senior vice president for business development. Past chair of the Randolph County Economic Development Corporation and member of the Randolph County Tax Commission. Degrees in accounting, finance and political science.
qual.why: Nearly six years of legislative service plus a finance and banking career and local tax and economic development work fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships and board seats were not counted.
qual.label: Nearly six years of legislative service plus a finance and banking career and local tax and economic development work fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships and board seats were not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will never vote to defund the police and will support law enforcement and first responders.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site lists the Second Amendment among the values he will fight for, with no specific policies given.

cands.name: Judy Little
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 29 in 2026. She ran for NC House District 55 in 2024 and for Wadesboro Town Council in 2019, losing each race. She attended West Stanly High School. No other career details were found.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended in 2026 by two Sway voting groups: The Civic Table (Carrie Jackson) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis). These are voter-guide recommendations, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We found no biography, occupation, birthplace, upbringing or date she moved to North Carolina. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2019, 2024 or 2026, so we found no stated positions on issues such as data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no campaign website, interviews or news coverage describing her platform or any controversy. Her record is limited to three losing campaigns, so there is no record of actions in office.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ballotpedia lists no occupation or work history. She has run for Wadesboro Town Council (2019, lost), NC House District 55 (2024, lost) and NC Senate District 29 (2026, lost), and has held no office.
qual.why: No career or office is documented, so job fit can't be scored.
